summary: This study describes the use of time-resolved Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to investigate the gas-phase dynamics during atomic layer deposition (ALD) of hafnium oxide (HfO2). The process involves the alternating injection of tetrakis(ethylmethylamido)hafnium (TEMAH) and water vapor, with the gas-phase dynamics monitored using FTIR. The study highlights the importance of mass transport and surface reactions in the ALD process and demonstrates the potential of time-resolved FTIR spectroscopy for understanding the behavior of ALD systems.
evidence: The text describes the use of time-resolved FTIR spectroscopy to study the gas-phase dynamics during the ALD of HfO2 using TEMAH and water. It also details the temperature conditions for the reactor components and the wafer chuck.
